questions.q: How does this lesson define Enterprise Architecture (EA)?
options: A certification specific to Salesforce administrators
The discipline of aligning an organization's technology landscape with its business strategy
A synonym for the Salesforce System Architect job title
A method for writing Apex code more efficiently
questions.explain: Enterprise Architecture is defined as the discipline that aligns an organization's systems, data, and applications with its business strategy -- a discipline that predates and extends beyond any single platform like Salesforce.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the four enterprise architecture layers this lesson describes?
options: Business, Data, Application, Technology
Security, Integration, Identity, Governance
Sales, Service, Marketing, Commerce
Development, Testing, Staging, Production
questions.explain: The lesson organizes enterprise architecture into business architecture (the 'why'), data architecture, application architecture, and technology architecture, each serving the layer above it.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the correct order of precedence when starting an enterprise architecture conversation?
options: Start with the technology layer, since infrastructure constraints should dictate business strategy
Start with whichever layer the loudest stakeholder prefers to discuss first
Start with business strategy and goals, and ensure every lower layer's decisions trace back to one of those goals
There is no correct order -- all four layers should be designed simultaneously with no sequence
questions.explain: The lesson insists business strategy comes first, with every application, data, and technology decision expected to trace back up to an actual business goal -- not the reverse order of starting from 'what can Salesforce do.'

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a System Architect be able to answer about any proposed integration, data model change, or system boundary decision?
options: How much the change will cost in licensing fees alone
Whether the change can be implemented within a single afternoon
Whether the change uses the newest available Salesforce feature
Which business goal the decision actually serves
questions.explain: The lesson states that a System Architect should always be able to trace a proposed change back to a specific business goal -- if the honest answer is 'none, it just seemed like good practice,' that signals the work has drifted from its purpose.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Salesforce System Architecture and the broader discipline of Enterprise Architecture?
options: System Architecture is a separate, unrelated discipline invented independently of Enterprise Architecture
A System Architect is applying the existing discipline of Enterprise Architecture specifically to how Salesforce fits into the business and systems landscape
Enterprise Architecture only applies to companies that have never implemented Salesforce
System Architecture replaces the need for Enterprise Architecture entirely once Salesforce is implemented
questions.explain: The lesson frames System Architecture as an application of the pre-existing Enterprise Architecture discipline to a Salesforce-specific context, not as an invented, separate practice.
